Date: 2026-07-09 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48m
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (CISO, Arcanum), Maya Chen (Cloud Security Lead), Diego Alvarez (Platform Engineer)
summary: Intro call to map Arcanum's security requirements for hosting LLM inference. Focus on SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, and retention policies. Discussed tradeoffs between Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private (VPC/on-prem). Agreed on sharing SOC2 snapshot and pricing ranges; pilot data set planned.
topics: Audit logging and retention / SIEM forwarding
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on this account. Priya my SE is with me. quick intro?
[00:08] Liam: Hi, Liam O'Connor, CISO for Arcanum Systems, we run analytics for supply chain, sensitive PII in parts of the pipeline. main thing is we need airtight controls and auditability.
[00:20] Priya: Hi all, Priya here, I focus on deployments and security posture, happy to walk technical details.
[00:30] Maya: Maya Chen, Cloud Security Lead. we use Okta for SSO, have a mix of AWS accounts in us-east-1 and eu-west-1, some data is euro-persistent and needs residency.
[00:42] Diego: Diego Alvarez, Platform Eng, I handle infra and secrets management.
[00:48] Jordan: Great. agenda — map requirements: SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, retention. then talk hosting options and what data flows look like. sound good?
[00:58] Liam: Yep. our timeline is Q3 pilot then decision by end of Q3. budget TBD but security is gating.
[01:12] Priya: Awesome, couple clarifying q's — when you say sensitive PII, is that raw payload hitting the model, or preprocessed?
[01:20] Liam: Both. Some flow raw, but we can tokenise or mask if needed. we need ability to ensure no PII persists in logs beyond retention.
[01:32] Diego: Also curious about key management — we currently use AWS KMS with multi-account keys. would prefer CMK if possible.
[01:42] Priya: Redwood supports customer-managed keys for Private deployments today, and Dedicated has options — for Hosted we offer BYOK via envelope encryption, but we should map specifics.
[01:55] Jordan: On SOC2, we are SOC2 Type II — we can share the report excerpt. that covers access controls, change mgmt, incident response — but we'll send a controls mapping specifically for hosted vs private differences.
[02:12] Maya: Do you have ISO27001 certification?
[02:16] Priya: We are in progress with ISO workstreams; have some scoping docs, not fully certified across all regions yet.
[02:24] Liam: Ok noted. can you explain audit logging granularity — request-level logs, user-level identity, api key tokens? we need forwardable logs to our Splunk.
[02:36] Priya: We emit structured request logs with request-id, model, model-version, token counts, and a user identifier when available. For Hosted we can stream syslog/forward to customer SIEM via secure forwarder; for Dedicated/Private you can ship logs locally. retention windows configurable per deployment tier.
[02:54] Diego: Are token payloads ever stored in logs? even obfuscated?
[02:58] Priya: By default we do not persist full request text in long-term logs for hosted; ephemeral traces may exist for debugging with redaction options. Dedicated/Private gives you total control — you can disable transcript storage.
[03:12] Jordan: Let's talk SSO. you said Okta. we support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM for provisioning. can integrate with Okta and map groups to RBAC roles.
[03:26] Maya: Group mappings are important — devs vs data-scientists vs security ops need different permissions; also need an ability to restrict model rollout to certain roles.
[03:36] Priya: Our Console supports RBAC with role templates; you can create custom roles, and API keys can be scoped to routes/models and have expiration. For Dedicated/Private you can enable stricter network policy and IP allowlists.
[03:51] Liam: Encryption at rest — can Redwood use our customer-managed KMS?
[03:56] Priya: Short answer: yes for Private, yes for Dedicated with KMS integration (we support AWS KMS and HSM integrations), Hosted supports BYOK with envelope keys but there are limitations around cross-region keys — we'll document.
[04:12] Diego: How about e2e encryption for traffic?
[04:15] Priya: TLS 1.2+/mTLS options for private peering. hosted uses TLS; for private connections we can do mTLS or VPC peering with privatelink-like setup. sometimes we see customers want IPsec tunnels for on-prem.
[04:30] Liam: Data residency and retention — we need certain PII to never leave eu-west-1. is that feasible?
[04:37] Jordan: Yes, we can pin deployments to regions. Dedicated capacity can be provisioned in eu-west; Private on-prem obviously stays local. Hosted can be region-restricted for enterprise customers.
[04:51] Maya: Retention windows — we need 30 days default for logs, with ability to archive for 7 years for audit. is that supported?
[04:58] Priya: We support configurable retention for logs and traces. seven years archival usually requires separate contract/add-on for long-term cold storage; we can push logs to customer's S3 or your archive location for retention.
[05:14] Diego: How about key rotation and revocation — if an API key is compromised, can we revoke and audit usage back to the offending token?
[05:22] Priya: Yes, we have immediate key rotation and revocation for API keys and support audit trails tying requests to key IDs. We also support short-lived tokens and session-based keys to reduce blast radius.
[05:36] Liam: Any regulatory audits you support? e.g., we have to show evidence for GDPR DPIA and some SOC controls.
[05:44] Jordan: We can provide artifact packages: SOC2 report, pen-test summary, encryption maps, data flow diagrams, and a controls mapping document. Priya will produce the controls mapping specific to how Hosted/Dedicated/Private meet controls.
[05:58] Maya: One concern — latency. If we go Dedicated in eu-west-1, what's typical p95? we need under 150ms for short-generation use cases.
[06:07] Priya: p95 depends on model and sequence length; for smaller 7B-style models p95 on dedicated optimized infra often <100ms for short calls, for larger 70B models it increases. we'll share benchmark sheet with similar workloads.
[06:22] Diego: For pilot we'd want to run a small benchmark with our prompts and measure both latency and token cost.
[06:29] Jordan: Absolutely — next step is to run a pilot on a ded or hosted variant and share a benchmark template.
[06:36] Liam: Regarding personnel access, we need audit logs showing who accessed what at the token level. is that available?
[06:44] Priya: We emit audit logs with user identifier, action (create model, deploy, read logs), and resource. For hosted, we include redacted request metadata; for Private, full fidelity.
[06:56] Maya: On SAML, do you support SCIM for group sync?
[06:59] Priya: Yes, SCIM supported in the Console for group provisioning and mapping to RBAC.
[07:06] Diego: Where do secrets live for hosted? in Redwood-managed HSM?
[07:10] Priya: In hosted we keep envelope keys with a Redwood KMS backed by cloud provider KMS and HSM, with BYOK options. For Dedicated/Private you can bring your own KMS/HSM and we can integrate.
[07:25] Jordan: Any known gaps? Priya: ISO isn't completed yet. we also have limited sovereign-region coverage in some pockets, will flag for ARCANUM if eu-residency is hard for a hosted tier.
[07:38] Liam: Good to know. security questionnaire — can we have a walkthrough of the questionnaire and fill gaps?
[07:45] Jordan: We'll send the security questionnaire and the controls mapping. Priya will follow up on technical integration steps.
[07:52] Maya: One more question — can we do an air-gapped on-prem deployment? we require for one of our subsidiaries.
[07:58] Priya: We offer a private on-prem package; it's more involved with installation, offline keys, and custom CA but it's supported. we'll share deployment playbook.
[08:08] Diego: Does private deployment still get Redwood console?
[08:11] Priya: Private includes a customer-controlled console, can be federated to your IdP. telemetry and usage can be pushed to your observability stack instead of Redwood's hosted analytics.
[08:22] Jordan: Any blockers on your side for moving to pilot?
[08:26] Liam: We need SOC2 artifacts and clarity on BYOK and regional hosting before sign-off from procurement, also cost ranges.
[08:36] Jordan: Understood. summary of next actions then: share SOC2 excerpt and mapping, pricing ranges, pilot benchmark template, and deployment playbook for private.
[08:47] Maya: We'll assemble a pilot dataset and internal stakeholders and aim to start the week of July 20.
[08:54] Jordan: Great. we'll follow up with calendar invites and links.
[09:00] [Speaker 1]: okay thanks everyone bye.
